newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain's CEPSA Q1 pretax profit up 32 percent.
newsitem.headline: Spain's CEPSA Q1 pretax profit up 32 percent.

text.p: Results for first quarter 1997, in billion pesetas unless stated:
NOTE - The firm added in a statement that first quarter conditions were not as negative as during the first quarter of 1996.

"Comparing the two, we must take into account the important investment effort in the past few years, the strict policy of cost contention and the increase in group activity in determined strategic segments," Cepsa said.
Although crude prices saw a downtrend in the first quarter versus the end of 1996, crude on average was up 13 percent versus the first quarter of 1996.
Average refining margins were slightly lower year on year, but this was offset by dollar strength, Cepsa said.
Marketing margins were slightly higher, reversing a recent trend.
Petroleum activities saw operating profit of more than 7.1 billion pesetas, up "notably" from the year-earlier period.
Group operating profit was up 16 percent to 10.49 billion pesetas, the firm added. That was after a 24 percent provision for depreciation.
Petrochemical sales rose eight percent, with operating profit for the division standing at 3.37 billion peseta. The firm said there were signs of an upturn in the cycle.

By divisions, Exploration and Production investment was 1.14 billion pesetas in the first quarter, Refining and Distribution investment was 3.98 billion pesetas, while Petrochemicals saw funds of 2.19 billion pesetas injected.
The firm said it planned to invest 40.6 billion pesetas in 1997.
